name: py-chunked
instruction: Implement chunked.py: def chunked(seq, n, strict=False). Yield successive lists of length n from seq. The final chunk may be shorter unless strict=True, in which case a short final chunk raises ValueError. n must be a positive int or ValueError. chunked must work LAZILY on any iterator (not just a list) and must not consume more of the source than needed — consuming one chunk from an infinite iterator must terminate. An empty source yields nothing.
gateCmd: python3 -c "from chunked import chunked as c; assert list(c([1,2,3],2))==[[1,2],[3]]; print('gate ok')"
verifyCmd:
python3 -c "from chunked import chunked as c
import itertools
assert list(c([1,2,3,4],2))==[[1,2],[3,4]]
assert list(c([1,2,3],2))==[[1,2],[3]]
assert list(c([],2))==[]
try:
    list(c([1,2,3],2,strict=True)); raise SystemExit('no ValueError strict')
except ValueError: pass
for bad in (0,-1):
    try:
        list(c([1],bad)); raise SystemExit('no ValueError n')
    except ValueError: pass
g=c(itertools.count(),3)
assert next(iter(g))==[0,1,2]
it=iter([1,2,3,4,5])
gen=c(it,2)
assert next(gen)==[1,2]
print('ok')"
